title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This page consolidates the canonical Platform Systems & Services runbooks, dashboard and alert conventions, common how-tos, recent retrospectives, and the 2026 roadmap for the Platform team. It is intended to be the first-stop reference for oncall engineers, owners of platform services, and engineers onboarding to platform operations.

Scope
- Systems covered: api-router, auth-proxy, ingress-controller, edge-cache, k8s-platform (control plane), job-queue, model-serving-gateway, metrics-ingest, alerting-pipeline.
- Topics: runbooks, dashboard definitions, alert thresholds, SLOs & error budget rules, triage playbooks, oncall handover, how-tos for common tasks, retrospective summaries, and roadmap items.

Ownership
- Platform systems owner: eng-platform (team leads: Aisha Patel, Marco Chen).
- Oncall rota: platform-oncall (primary / secondary).
- Alerts & dashboard ownership: assigned per-service in the platform team roster (see Team Wiki section for current assignment table).

SLOs & Error Budgets (current)
- api-router: availability 99.95% monthly; p99 latency < 250ms for production traffic.
- k8s-platform API: availability 99.9% monthly; control-plane API error rate < 0.5% sustained.
- model-serving-gateway: request success rate 99.9% (excluding client-side validation errors); p95 latency < 300ms.
- Error budget policy: Any service that spends > 50% of its monthly error budget triggers a mandatory retrospec and prioritized mitigation plan.

Dashboards & Alerting (standard conventions)
- Dashboard layout (one per service):
  1) Overview: throughput (rps), 95/99 latency, error rate, active host count, CPU/GPU utilization.
  2) Health: container restarts, OOMs, crashloops, rate limit breaches.
  3) Performance: queue depth, request size distribution, p50/p95/p99 latencies by route.
  4) Capacity: pod counts, node utilization, autoscaler events.
  5) Traces & logs: sample traces and recent error logs.

- Alert naming convention: platform.<service>.<severity>.<condition> (e.g., platform.api-router.sev1.high-5xx-rate).
- Alert severity mapping:
  - sev1: paging, requires immediate acknowledgement within 5 minutes (critical customer impact or total service outage).
  - sev2: oncall must acknowledge within 15 minutes (degraded but partial service).
  - sev3: ticketed, handled during business hours (no immediate customer impact).

Key alert thresholds (examples)
- platform.api-router.sev1.high-5xx-rate: 5xx rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes across production.
- platform.model-serving-gateway.sev1.p95-latency: p95 latency > 800ms for 5 minutes.
- platform.k8s-platform.sev1.apiserver-error: apiserver 5xx > 0.5% for 3 minutes OR apiserver unresponsive > 30s.
- platform.gpu-pool.sev2.high-util: average GPU utilization > 85% for 10 minutes (risk of capacity starvation).
- platform.ingress-controller.sev2.rate-limit: upstream 429s > 3% for 10 minutes.

Runbooks (operational playbooks)
1) Runbook: api-router high 5xx rate (platform.api-router.sev1.high-5xx-rate)
  - Purpose: Restore production request success rate and identify root cause.
  - Pager response checklist:
    a) Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty and update Slack #platform-incident channel with initial diagnosis timeline.
    b) Run: curl to the health endpoint behind the router and directly to a backend to compare responses. Example commands:
       - curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood-inference.com/health | head
       - kubectl -n production exec -c api-router $(kubectl -n production get pods -l app=api-router -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/metrics | head
    c) Check Dashboard: error-rate by route, recent deploys (CI/CD), and host-level OOMs/restarts.
    d) If new deploy in last 30 minutes: rollback using CI job (Jenkins/GHA) labeled "api-router:rollback" and watch traffic.
    e) If error is traffic surge or upstream timeout: enable emergency rate limiting via ingress config and notify product.
    f) If container OOM/crashloop: scale down new pods and pin previous stable revision.
    g) Create a post-incident ticket with timeline, root cause, and short-term fix. Assign for retrospective if error budget >50%.

2) Runbook: model-serving-gateway high latency (platform.model-serving-gateway.sev1.p95-latency)
  - Quick checks:
    - Check Redis/KV cache hit rate for model prefix caching.
    - Verify GPU node health and NVidia driver logs.
    - Inspect batching subsystem: if batching queue depth spikes, consider temporarily lowering batch window.
  - Commands:
    - kubectl -n model get pods -l app=model-serving-gateway -o wide
    - kubectl logs -n model -l app=model-serving-gateway --tail=200 | grep -i error
  - Escalation: If persistent and affects >25% of traffic, escalate to runtime team and open a P0 Slack channel.

How-Tos (common operational tasks)
- Deploy rollback (safe path):
  1) Identify failing release tag in CI (GHA).
  2) Trigger rollout to previous stable tag via: gh workflow run rollback.yml --field service=api-router --field tag=sha1234
  3) Verify health in Dashboard for 10 minutes, confirm p95 latency and error rate falling.

- Adding a new dashboard panel (Grafana):
  1) Clone service dashboard, set panel title and PromQL query, add panel-level thresholds (warning/critical) that map to sev2/sev1 alerts.
  2) Commit panel JSON to infra/grafana/dashboards/<service>.json and open PR against infra-configs.
  3) Request review from dashboard owner.

- Creating an alert rule (Prometheus Alertmanager):
  1) Author alert in yaml under infra/alerting/<service>.yaml following naming convention.
  2) Include runbook link and pager escalation policy in the alert labels. Example:
     - alert: platform_api_router_high_5xx_rate
       expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api-router\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api-router\"}[5m])) > 0.05
       for: 5m
       labels:
         severity: "sev1"
         team: "platform"

Retrospectives (recent summaries)
- Incident 2025-12-14: api-router increased 5xx after a middleware change. Root cause: improper header handling introduced in library v2.1. Fix: rollback and validation tests added. Action items: add integration test for header edge-cases, update SDK.
- Incident 2026-01-22: batch job-queue backlog due to malformed payloads from partner ingestion pipeline. Root cause: missing validation at ingress. Fix: added JSON schema validation and reject + DLQ. Action items: partner contract update and more aggressive input validation.

Roadmap (Q2-Q4 2026)
- Q2 2026:
  - Migrate all platform dashboards to unified templated Grafana dashboards (task: PF-234).
  - Implement autoscaling policies that consider GPU memory pressure for model-serving clusters (PF-240).
  - Add circuit-breaker support in api-router for upstream degeneration.
- Q3 2026:
  - Ship unified observability pipeline (traces + logs + metrics in a single pane).
  - Rollout automated canary analysis for every platform deployment.
- Q4 2026:
  - Improve SLO-driven capacity planner that recommends reserved capacity for Dedicated customers.
  - Run a business continuity game day for platform private deployments.

Team Wiki & Onboarding links
- Canonical owner roster and oncall schedule: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q2
- CI/CD playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-operations-playbook-2026-q1
- Runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026.json

Post-Incident Followup & Retrospective Process
- When an incident breaches severity or error budget thresholds, owner must schedule a blameless retro within 7 business days. Retro template: timeline, detection, mitigation, root cause, contributing factors, action items with owners and target dates.
- Action items are tracked in the platform action board (Jira project PF) with labels: incident, action-item, retro.

Appendices
- Useful commands and snippets:
  - kubectl contexts: kubectl config use-context prod && kubectl -n production get pods -l app=api-router
  - PromQL snippet for error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~\"api-router|model-serving-gateway\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~\"api-router|model-serving-gateway\"}[5m]))

- Contacts and escalation matrix:
  - Platform oncall primary: platform-oncall-primary@redwood-inference.com
  - Runtime escalation: runtime-team@redwood-inference.com
  - Incident commander rotation: see team wiki roster.

Notes
- This document is reviewed quarterly and after any sev1 incident. For changes to alert thresholds or SLOs, submit a PR and request review from the SRE lead.

References
- See related pages (dashboards, runbooks, playbooks) in the Team Wiki and infra repos for exact panel JSON and alert YAML examples.
